thread:
marina: Quick sync — enterprise customers are asking for explicit "pin contracts" when a model is scheduled for sunset. They want written guarantees about cutoff dates, migration windows, and rollback options. Can we capture what product needs to sign off on?

devon: From eng-ml perspective: we need a minimal benchmark matrix before we promise anything. At least: 99p latency, token-cost delta, top-1 regression on the primary eval suite, and hallucination/factuality delta on customer prompts.

sana: +1. Also need an operational gate: must have a migration playbook with automated reroute and an opt-in fallback for pinned customers. Otherwise SLA risk.

tyler: Sales note — two large customers already asked for a 6mo pin window. They'll push on compensation if we can't guarantee perf parity. We should define a template for commercial exceptions.

ev an: (cust-succ) spelled out what customers actually mean by "pin" — they want: 1) guaranteed traffic on old model instance, 2) an upgrade path with testing, 3) a clear deprecation date and rollback runbook.

devon: For #1 we can support pinned legacy instances but it's a capacity+cost commitment. Need a simple pricing addendum and an autoscaler override. For #2 we need a customer sandbox that mirrors their production inputs for validation.

marina: Can we draft a short checklist that product/legal/sales/eng can agree on? Something we can attach to SOWs. Suggested sections: Scope (models + versions), Benchmarks (eval names + thresholds), Window (start/end), Ops (rollback + opt-out), Pricing & credits, Escalation path.

legal-bot: Heads up — any formal "guarantee" language will trigger additional indemnity & audit requirements. Recommend limiting to "reasonable efforts" where possible and specifying measurable gates.

sana: Good call. Proposal: keep customer-facing doc simple and prescriptive (tables + timelines), keep legal appendix with measured gates. Product owns the customer doc, eng-ml owns benchmark spec, sales owns commercial template.

tyler: I'll draft the commercial template if you draft the SOW checklist. Also need a short line for AE handoff that explains what to collect from customer (sample prompts, SLO targets, traffic percent).

devon: For the benchmark spec I'll propose these concrete artifacts to include in the SOW: 

```
- Eval suite name(s): e.g., prod-api-regression-v2, hallucination-checklist-2025
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, relative token-cost %, top-1 exact-match delta, hallucination-rate (annotated sample)
- Acceptance rule: no more than 5% degradation on top-1 and <1% absolute hallucination increase on customer-critical prompts
```

sana: Nice. Can we also capture the hard launch gate: "benchmarks + successful sandbox run (1M tokens) + runbook drill (2 simulated failovers)"? That makes the risk assessment concrete.

ev an: That drill will reassure customers. Also please add a coms checklist: migration notice cadence, sample rollback messages, support POC list.

marina: Action items: sana to synth the customer-facing SOW checklist by EOD Wed; devon to write benchmark spec doc link and validation steps; tyler to draft commercial exception template; evan to write comms checklist. I'll collate and loop legal for the appendix on Thurs.

tyler: FYI I'll ping AE for the two customers and offer temporary credits during their migration window. :+1:

legal-bot: When drafting appendix, include a clause for "pinned instance termination" with minimum 30d notice and an emergency rollback SLA.

marina: Thanks team — we'll reconvene Friday for sign-off. If anyone wants to add items to the checklist, drop them here.
